text:
erin: FYI customer 'Acme Editor' says lots of streaming sessions are getting counted as 5xx when users disconnect mid-chunk. example request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. they see EPIPE on the proxy but runtime logs a successful 200 and tokens sent. billing team is getting escalations.

sam: which region and plan? hosted only or also dedicated? :thinking_face:

erin: hosted, us-west-2. customer on free tier first noticed it but also repros on paid org. repro steps below (they gave a tiny script). can we reproduce locally?

mike: throwing a quick log snippet from our gateway for the request-id:

```
2026-03-15T18:02:12.341Z gateway[gw-12]: req=req_0a1b2c3d upstream_write=OK upstream_status=200 tokens=312
2026-03-15T18:02:12.342Z gateway[gw-12]: socket: write returned EPIPE (errno=32)
2026-03-15T18:02:12.342Z gateway[gw-12]: connection: client reset by peer (RST) after write
2026-03-15T18:02:12.343Z gateway[gw-12]: meter: classify_request_as_5xx req=req_0a1b2c3d reason=client_conn_teardown
```

mike: so upstream succeeded but classifier still flagged as 5xx because connection teardown was seen as an error path.

sam: can you paste the customer's repro (curl)? sometimes clients send Transfer-Encoding: chunked and then close connection mid-chunk. if the proxy treats any socket error after write as up-error we mark 5xx. quick repro (from customer):

```
# quick repro: open a streaming POST, send initial chunk then close socket immediately
curl -v "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d $'5\r\nhello\r\n6\r\n world\r\n' --no-buffer --raw
# then kill the curl process before finishing final chunk
```

erin: customer says they abort after receiving a few tokens (UX event) so they intentionally close early. they expect it to be counted as client abort (no 5xx). billing shows as provider 5xx which is triggering refunds.

mike: quick analysis: our current heuristic marks a request as 5xx if the connection ends with an EPIPE or other write error during streaming. that catches server-side failures but also catches normal client aborts. we need to differentiate: if upstream already returned 2xx (or wrote bytes) then treat as client abort for billing/alerts.

sam: two actionable checks we can do:
- check runtime/upstream final status before classifying (if >=200 && <500 and bytes_sent>0, prefer client-abort)
- inspect tcp teardown semantics: FIN from client vs RST. RST tends to imply abrupt reset; FIN can be graceful. but many proxies see both as 'closed' and surface EPIPE.

mike: right. also watch out for TLS-proxied clients where the proxy only sees connection close (no explicit RST flag). but we do have socket errno and write-return semantics and we have bytes_sent metric. short term patch: defer marking 5xx for N ms after upstream finish, and if upstream status OK and bytes_sent>0 mark as client_abort.

erin: ops/billing need concrete proposal and test cases to sign off. can you create a small unit/integration test that simulates: upstream-200+body then client closes -> should be client_abort; upstream-5xx then client close -> should be 5xx.

sam: i'll own the tests. plan: add integration harness that spins up a fake runtime which can be instructed to respond with 200+chunked and then keep connection open, then a client that closes mid-stream. assert classification.

mike: patch proposal: change gateway/metering/classifier: only mark provider 5xx on socket write errors if upstream_status is >=500 OR bytes_sent==0 OR (socket_errno in {ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT} AND upstream_incomplete). otherwise mark as client_abort. will open PR.

erin: customer-facing messaging? ops-bot created TICKET-8947 for Acme Editor and tagged billing. i'll add repro steps to the ticket and tell them we expect a fix in the next deploy.

ops-bot: Created ticket TICKET-8947 and assigned to @sam, priority=P2.

erin: quick note for oncall: if you see a surge of these in production, do NOT auto-trigger provider-5xx pager unless upstream_status shows error or bytes_sent==0. i'll add that to runbook after PR lands.

sam: PR link and tests will be posted here in ~2h. tagging @mike for review. :thumbsup:

mike: sounds good. also logging suggestion: add metric "streaming_client_abort_count" separate from provider_5xx so we can monitor client behavior without conflating.

erin: agreed. putting this on the support->eng handoff doc. thanks everyone.

sam: pulling a quick repro result locally: when upstream=200 and client closed, gateway classifier now tags as client_abort in my local change. will push next.

mike: assigning follow-ups: sam -> tests + PR, mike -> review + add metric, erin -> customer comms + ticket updates.

erin: closing loop: customer verified temporary workaround (tweak in their client to send final zero-length chunk) but they prefer we handle server-side. will update TICKET-8947 when PR is merged.
